title: Auto queue toggle: UI button to enable/disable automatic worker dispatch
description:
Add a button in the dashboard Workers section that toggles "auto queue" on and off. When enabled, a background worker polls for claimable tasks: if a task can be claimed and a runner slot is free (respecting worker limit / loop.maxParallel), it dispatches a worker to run it; if nothing is claimable, it sleeps (wait 1 min or more) before polling again. When disabled, no automatic dispatch happens, matching current manual behavior.

This is the explicit on/off control and wait-then-poll behavior that am-8wd (auto-pick) implies but does not specify: am-8wd keeps every free slot filled via an always-on server loop; this task adds the user-facing toggle and the idle-backoff so the auto queue can be disabled and does not hammer bd while the queue is empty.

Related: am-8wd (auto-pick kanban), am-xey (triage of unclaimable tasks).

### How to use

Toggle Auto queue in the Workers section of the dashboard. With it on, free runner slots get filled automatically as tasks become claimable, polling with a backoff of at least 1 minute when there is nothing to claim; with it off, dispatch is manual as today.

title: am-9h4 stuck in_progress despite PR #30 merged: reconcile never closes the tracker bead
description:
REPORT: why am-9h4 shows in_progress although already merged and completed

am-9h4's PR #30 was merged (commit 3dd4763, 2026-09-21 01:23 +0200). Internally the task IS done: the store row is state=done, reason='PR merged' (packages/core/src/reconcile.ts:32), set by the PR-poller at 01:27. Yet the bead is still in_progress with no explicit blockers (bd show lists no dependencies).

Root cause: reconcilePrs (packages/core/src/reconcile.ts) only appends a task.state event to the local SQLite store. It never calls tracker.close(id) / tracker.setStatus(id,'closed') to update the actual tracker. Grep finds no production caller of tracker.close/setStatus at all; the runner only calls tracker.release() on cancel. The beads issue therefore keeps the claim-time in_progress status forever (heartbeats continued until 02:29:44, then the lease expired and left it parked in_progress).

Fix: reconcilePrs should close the tracker issue when a PR merges (and setStatus/release on abandoned/closed-without-merge), so a settled PR surfaces as closed in beads. The poller test (packages/server/src/pr-poller.test.ts) asserts only the store state, so it never caught this.

title: Command to check GitHub PRs for merge conflicts and dispatch agent to resolve them

Provide a command that:

1. Lists current GitHub pull requests (repo: mcpie87/amagi, origin remote).
2. Checks each PR for merge conflicts against origin/main (via gh, e.g. mergeable/mergeStateStatus).
3. If a merge conflict is present, dispatches an agent (opencode run) with a task relevant to that PR to resolve the conflict vs origin/main.

### How to use

Run `bun run packages/cli/src/index.ts check-prs` from the repo root. It lists all open GitHub PRs with their merge state (CLEAN / CONFLICT / UNKNOWN) against the configured base branch, then for each conflicting PR it creates a worktree off the PR head, merges the base branch in, and dispatches an opencode agent to resolve the conflicts and commit. The resolved merge is pushed back to the PR head ref, updating the PR. Pass `--dry-run` to only list PRs and conflicts without dispatching agents.
acceptance_criteria: - Command lists PRs and reports merge-conflict state.\n- On conflict, an agent is dispatched per PR with a task referencing the PR.\n- Agent attempts resolution against origin/main.

title: Runner opens a pull request even when the diff against base is empty
description:
Observed on PR #113: zero file changes, nothing to merge.

Runner.drive gates pull request creation on commit() (packages/core/src/runner.ts:364), and
commit() only checks `git status --porcelain` on the worktree (runner.ts:668-670). A dirty
tree means a commit, and a commit means openPullRequest. Nothing between those two points
asks whether the commit actually adds anything relative to the base branch.

openPullRequest then calls changesSinceBase (packages/core/src/pr-body.ts:23), which runs
`git diff --numstat origin/<base>...HEAD`. When that returns an empty list the code carries
on regardless: formatPrBody just omits the '### What changed' section (pr-body.ts:120-128)
and the pull request opens with a body that describes work the diff does not contain.

This happens when the worktree branched from a stale base and the agent re-applied a change
that had already landed on main, so the three-dot diff against the merge base is empty even
though the worktree was dirty and the commit is real.

Fix: in openPullRequest, after changesSinceBase, bail when changes.length === 0. Do not call
forge.createPr, do not push (the push lives inside createPr, pr.ts:64-95, so skipping the
call skips the push too, and there is nothing worth pushing: an empty three-dot diff means
the commit adds nothing over the merge base). Transition the task to no_pr with a reason
naming the real cause, e.g. 'the agent committed, but the diff against <base> is empty; the
work is probably already on <base>'. That reason must be distinguishable from the existing
'produced no changes' string (runner.ts:387), because the two mean different things: one is
an agent that did nothing, this one is an agent that duplicated existing work.

Related: am-6hd (the opposite failure, real commits routed to no_pr), am-9ew (PR body
promises work the diff does not contain). This bug is upstream of the whole 'who closes a
pointless PR' policy: a creation-time gate means the pull request never exists.
design:
Gate at creation rather than cleaning up afterwards. It kills the entire class before a
human or a watcher ever sees a pull request. It cannot catch a pull request that becomes
empty later (base moved, work superseded); that case is the watcher's job and is filed
separately.
acceptance_criteria:
* openPullRequest does not call forge.createPr when changesSinceBase returns an empty list.
* No branch is pushed in that case.
* The task lands in no_pr with a reason that names the empty diff and is distinct from the existing no-changes string.
* runner.test.ts covers: dirty worktree + empty diff against base -> no_pr, no createPr call, no push.
* The existing dirty worktree + non-empty diff -> pr_open path is unchanged.

title: PR body needs an agent-authored conclusion about the actual diff, not just the task description
description:
formatPrBody (packages/core/src/pr-body.ts:110) builds the whole PR body from the
tracker description plus a numstat file list. Everything a reviewer reads (the
Summary section) is a restatement of the task as it was written before any code
existed; the only diff-derived part is the bare `- path +N -M` list. Nothing in
the body says what the changed files actually do.

Observed on PR #114 (am-b2z.8.2, kanban board scrolling): the Summary promised
horizontal and per-column scrolling via CSS overflow, while the entire diff was
`justfile +9 -0`. The body still read as a plausible PR because the summary never
had to agree with the diff.

Add a conclusion section, authored by the implementing agent after the work is
done, describing what the changes do file by file and calling out anything the
reviewer needs to know (deviations from the task, what was left out, why a file
that looks unrelated was touched).

Work needed:

* Prompt: extend the rule at packages/core/src/prompt.ts:25 so the agent appends a
  `### Conclusion` section to the tracker description once the work is finished,
  written against the real diff (`git diff <base>...HEAD`), not against the task.
  It is mandatory for every PR, unlike the optional `### How to use`.
* pr-body: generalize splitDescription (pr-body.ts:47) - it currently splits on a
  single hardcoded `### How to use` heading - to also pull out `### Conclusion`,
  and render it in formatPrBody after the `### 🛠️ What changed` list, so the
  reviewer reads the file list and then what those files do.
* Fallback: when the agent wrote no conclusion, use the run's final-message
  summary (already captured as the no-PR reason, see prompt.ts:29) rather than
  emitting the section empty or silently dropping it.
* Tests: pr-body.test.ts for the new split and ordering, prompt.test.ts for the
  new instruction, runner.test.ts for the end-to-end body.

Why: reviewers work from the diff. A PR body that only paraphrases the task
description gives them nothing to check the diff against, and hides the case
where the diff does not match the task at all.
acceptance_criteria:
* Every generated PR body has a conclusion section describing what the changed
  files do, placed after the What changed file list.
* The conclusion is written after implementation against the real diff, not copied
  from the task description.
* When the agent supplied no conclusion, the run's final summary is used instead;
  the section is never rendered empty.
* `### How to use` keeps working as before, and a description with both sections
  splits correctly.

title: Give needs_human a real reason instead of bare "exit N"
description:

Claude Code writes almost nothing to stderr and emits no summary on a hard failure, so the fallback is what the operator sees in the dashboard and TUI. runner.ts:627 then stores that string verbatim as the needs_human reason.

Make the reason reconstructable from what we already capture: the agent.stream events and agent.exited are in the store, so the last assistant text, the last tool error, or the harness result message should be mined for a human-readable cause before falling back to the exit code. If nothing better exists, the reason should at least say which phase failed (implement / checks / commit / PR) and point at where to read the log.
acceptance_criteria:
- A failed agent run parks the task with a reason naming the actual cause, not just an exit code

- Dashboard task detail for am-tja-style failures shows something an operator can act on
- Covered by runner tests for: stderr present, summary present, stream-only signal, nothing at all

title: Doom-loop detection: catch busy-but-not-progressing agents
description:
The stall watcher only sees inactivity; an agent stuck re-running the same failing test or re-editing the same file forever keeps heartbeating and never trips it. Add a progress heuristic over the agent event stream: repeated near-identical tool calls (same command/file within a sliding window), N consecutive check rounds with an identical failure signature, or no change to the worktree diff over a time/turn window. Trip the guard and stop the run instead of letting it burn budget.

### How to use

The doom-loop guard extends the per-repo stall watcher inside `amagi serve` and runs on the same tick (`loop.stallWatchIntervalSec`). It is on by default (`loop.doomEnabled = true`) and scans every task with a live worker for three progress signals, configurable under `[loop]`:

- `doomToolWindowSec` (default 600) and `doomToolRepeat` (default 20): repeated near-identical tool calls, same command or file, within the window trip the guard.
- `doomCheckRounds` (default 3): consecutive check rounds sharing one failure signature trip the guard.
- `doomDiffWindowSec` (default 1800): a live worker whose worktree diff has not changed for this long trips the guard.

When a signal trips, the guard releases the tracker claim (the runner detects the lost lease and stops), appends a `doom.detected` event (kind `tool_repeat` / `check_repeat` / `diff_static`) and parks the task in `needs_human` with the reason, so a human reviews instead of the next worker re-burning budget. Set `loop.doomEnabled = false` to disable.
acceptance_criteria: Progress tracker fed from agent-log events with configurable window and thresholds; detection is unit-tested against synthetic event streams for both a looping and a genuinely slow-but-progressing run; a tripped guard emits a distinct event kind and moves the task out of implementing/fixing rather than silently killing it.

title: Context budget guard: stop or escalate a run before it hits the dumb zone
description:
Both harness translators already emit usage events (inputTokens/outputTokens/cachedTokens, cost for claude), but nothing acts on them. Track cumulative context size per run in the runner and enforce configurable thresholds: warn at a soft limit, act at a hard limit (default around 200k input tokens, per-harness override since context windows differ). Acting means ending the current agent process cleanly rather than letting it degrade.

### How to use

The runner now observes the harness usage events and records the run's peak input context (input + cached tokens) per task. Thresholds live under `[loop]` in `.amagi/config.toml` (or the global config):

```toml
[loop]
contextWarnTokens = 160000   # soft limit: logs a context.warn event once the run's peak context reaches it
contextMaxTokens = 200000    # hard limit: kills the agent and routes the task to needs_human when crossed

# Optional per-harness overrides (context windows differ per harness)
[loop.contextOverrides.codex]
maxTokens = 128000
```

Defaults: warn at 160k input tokens, hard stop at 200k, no overrides. On a hard crossing the runner appends a `context.exceeded` event, terminates the current agent process, and parks the task in `needs_human` with a reason stating the peak context and the limit; the worktree is preserved for a resumed run. `run.context` events record the running peak so health surfacing (am-672.5) can read it.
acceptance_criteria: Config keys under [loop] (e.g. contextWarnTokens, contextMaxTokens) with sane defaults; runner observes usage events and records peak context per run in the store; crossing the soft limit logs a warning event; crossing the hard limit terminates the agent and routes the task to the restart or needs_human path; unit tests drive the thresholds off fixture usage events.

title: Agent runaway safeguards: doom-loop and context-blowout guards
description: A worker agent can burn a whole session without making progress: repeating the same edit/test cycle, re-reading the same files, or growing its context past the point where quality collapses (the ~200k 'dumb zone'). Today the only guards are the stall watcher (wall-clock inactivity), loop.maxRetries for transient harness failures, and maxReviewRounds/maxCheckRounds. None of them catch an agent that is busy but useless. This epic adds progress-, budget- and context-aware safety rails that stop or escalate such runs instead of letting them grind.
design: Guard categories: (1) context/token budget from harness usage events, (2) no-progress/doom-loop heuristics, (3) hard wall-clock and cost budgets per task, (4) visibility in dashboard/TUI, (5) recovery via fresh-context restart rather than plain kill.

title: no_pr transition triggers even when agent already committed real changes, losing the PR
description:
Dashboard shows a task in 'needs_human'/no_pr state whose agent summary clearly describes real code changes (e.g. am-06j: 7 files, +122/-9, with detailed file-by-file breakdown) — but no PR exists, so it's unclear where the work went.

Root cause: runner.ts commit() (packages/core/src/runner.ts:635-653) only checks `git status --porcelain` on the worktree. If the agent already ran its own 'git commit' during the session (a common agent behavior, and something our own prompts/system-prompt don't forbid), the worktree is clean by the time commit() runs. commit() then returns false, and the caller (runner.ts:334-361) treats that as 'no changes were made', routing the task to no_pr and surfacing the agent's own summary as the 'reason' for having made no changes — even though the summary is describing changes that DID happen and ARE sitting in an unpushed commit in the worktree.

Fix direction: commit() (or its caller) needs to also check whether HEAD is ahead of the base branch (an existing unpushed commit), not just whether the working tree is dirty. If HEAD is ahead, treat it like the committed path (push + open PR) instead of falling into the no_pr branch. title: Worker: triage any unclaimed task and decide what to do with it
description:
The runner only ever claims the next ready task via `bd ready --claim --exclude-type epic,milestone,gate --exclude-label human`, so anything not directly claimable is invisible: epics sit open, finished epics stay open, orphaned tasks go untouched. Give this project (amagi itself) a triage driver that picks any unclaimed task not currently blocked by a worker in progress and decides the right action: implement it (claim and run), decompose it (break an epic/container into concrete subtasks), close it (children all done, or work already satisfied), ask the operator, or explicitly skip it with a recorded reason. The decider is a worker role separate from the implementation runner; it never runs the code itself.

### How to use

`amagi triage` picks one unclaimed task the runner skips (epics, milestones, blocked, orphaned tasks) and decides what to do with it. Run it from the repo root; it uses the `harness.triage` harness (default claude) unless `--harness`/`--model`/`--effort` override it.

- `implement` claims the task and hands it to the implementation runner (`amagi run`'s loop).
- `decompose` creates concrete subtasks under the container (epic/milestone) via `bd create --parent`.
- `close` closes the task with the recorded reason; it fails safely if the container still has open children.
- `ask` posts a question on the task (surfaced in the dashboard Inbox and as a `question.asked` event); once the operator answers, the next `amagi triage` pass acts on that answer.
- `skip` records the reason as a comment on the task.

Every decision is written as a `triage.decision` event in the store. Leaf tasks are triaged once; a decomposed container is re-triaged only after all its children close, so finished epics get closed. The server also exposes `POST /api/repos/:repo/triage` to trigger a pass for a repo.
acceptance_criteria: A triage entrypoint scans unclaimed tasks (open, not in_progress, not held by a live worker lease) in this project and picks one. For each candidate it records a decision: implement, decompose, close, ask, or skip-with-reason. An epic with only closed children gets closed; an epic with no children gets decomposed into subtasks instead of ignored. The decision and its rationale are visible in the dashboard and tracker.

title: Isolate forge credentials from operators and harness agents
description:
Replace the human-only gh/tea login prerequisite with token-only, non-interactive forge access. GH must use Chise's token from the Amagi process environment without gh auth state. Tea must either use a dedicated Amagi XDG config profile provisioned by the program from a token, or be replaced with a direct token-authenticated Forgejo client. Harness agents must never inherit forge credentials.

### How to use

Token-only forge access, no `gh auth login` or `tea login` step. Export the bot token into the Amagi process environment before running `amagi serve`/`amagi run`:

- GitHub: `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Forgejo: `FORGEJO_TOKEN` (optionally `GITEA_SERVER_URL`; otherwise the repo origin remote supplies the server URL).

Amagi runs `gh` against its own `GH_CONFIG_DIR` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/amagi/forge/github`) with the token, never the operator's auth state, and rewrites the git remote to push/fetch over HTTPS with the token. For Forgejo, Amagi provisions a dedicated tea login (`amagi`) into `$XDG_STATE_HOME/amagi/forge/tea` and opens PRs through a direct token-authenticated Forgejo API client.

Harness agents never inherit forge credentials: token env vars are stripped and agents get an empty `GH_CONFIG_DIR` plus an XDG config profile that mirrors the operator's except for the gh/tea dirs, so an agent reaching for the forge fails closed.

`amagi repos`/`amagi add` report a new `forge <kind> token` readiness check naming the missing env var.

title: PrDriver.closePr and a dashboard close action for flagged pull requests
description:
Nothing in amagi can close a pull request. PrDriver is exactly createPr, getPr,
listComments, postComment (packages/core/src/drivers/pr.ts:32-40); there is no gh pr close,
pr merge, pr edit or pr reopen anywhere in the repo. So when the watcher flags a pull
request as pointless (am-2oo.4), the operator has to leave the dashboard, find the pull
request on the forge, and close it there.

Add closePr to PrDriver and wire it to a dashboard action only.

Explicitly not wired to: the watcher, the runner, or any agent. Amagi flags and a human
closes (the policy recorded in am-2oo.4); this issue only removes the context switch, it
does not change who decides.

Work needed:

* PrDriver.closePr(cwd, number, reason). gh driver: gh pr close with a closing comment.
  Forgejo driver: PATCH repos/<slug>/pulls/<n> {state: 'closed'}, matching the direct-API
  approach the rest of the forgejo driver already uses (pr.ts:150-155 explains why tea is
  bypassed for the pull request lifecycle).
* Server endpoint. The shape to reuse is POST /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/close shipped in
  am-0c3 (packages/server/src/app.ts:407-470), which already takes an operator reason and a
  target state and calls tracker.close. Extend it, or add a sibling, so that closing a task
  in pr_flagged also closes the pull request rather than leaving it open on the forge.
* Dashboard: a close action on the task detail view for pr_flagged tasks, showing the
  watcher's reasoning comment inline so the operator decides against the evidence rather
  than going to look it up.
* Guard: closing is only offered for pr_flagged. A pr_open task with a live diff must not
  get a close button.

Out of scope: a TUI close action, and any bulk-close over the attention list. Both are
worth doing if flagged pull requests ever pile up; neither is worth doing now.
design:
Dashboard-only on purpose. Building closePr does not weaken the flag-do-not-close policy
as long as the only caller is an operator click; making it callable from a watcher would.
acceptance_criteria:
* PrDriver exposes closePr and both the gh and forgejo drivers implement it.
* Closing a pr_flagged task from the dashboard closes the pull request on the forge, records the operator's reason, moves the task to abandoned, and closes the tracker issue.
* The watcher, the runner and the harness agents have no path to closePr.
* The close action is not offered for pr_open tasks.
* The watcher's reasoning is visible on the same screen as the close action.

title: PR watcher: flag pointless pull requests with a label and reasoning, never close them
description:
Amagi has no post-creation check for whether an open pull request is still worth
anything. check-prs only reads mergeable/mergeStateStatus (packages/core/src/pr-check.ts:27-32);
an empty pull request shows as CLEAN, gets filtered out, and the command prints 'no merge
conflicts'. reconcile.ts only reacts after a human merges or closes. Nothing asks 'does this
diff do anything'.

Add a pointlessness pass to the shared PR watcher (see am-2oo.1: one listOpenPrs per tick,
conflict + reconciliation + pointlessness checks over the same list, rather than three
pollers hammering the same endpoint).

Policy: amagi flags, a human closes. Auto-close was rejected on attention, not
reversibility: a closed pull request stops being looked at, so a wrong close is a silently
lost pull request, while a wrong label is a two-second dismissal. The pre-pull-request half
already made this call, the no_pr reason string tells the operator to verify and close
explicitly; auto-closing once a pull request exists would make amagi more aggressive with
real work on the table than it is with none.

Scope of the check:

* Applies only to pull requests carrying the 'amagi' provenance label (drivers/pr.ts:14).
  Amagi must never comment on or flag a pull request a human opened. Note this filter is
  deliberately different from the conflict check in the same watcher, which applies to any
  pull request against the base branch.
* v1 criterion is empty diff only: the diff against base is empty. This already subsumes
  the superseded case, because work that landed on base by another route makes the
  three-dot diff go empty by itself. Staleness is explicitly out of scope: an old pull
  request is not a pointless one.
* Mechanical evidence only. No model reads the diff and judges it against the task.
  'This diff does not do what the task asked' is a separate, harder problem that belongs
  with am-9ew.

On flag:

* Add the 'amagi/needs-closing' label to the pull request.
* Post a comment on the pull request with the reasoning, because that is where the close
  button is and where the decision gets made.
* Post the same reasoning as a comment on the tracker issue, so it survives after the pull
  request is gone. This satisfies am-6ap.
* Transition the task pr_open -> pr_flagged.

On clear (a later tick finds the pull request no longer qualifies, e.g. someone pushed real
commits to it):

* Remove the 'amagi/needs-closing' label.
* Transition pr_flagged -> pr_open.
* Do not post another comment; the label going away is the signal.

Work needed:

* PrDriver gains label mutation on an existing pull request. Today amagiLabels
  (drivers/pr.ts:16-19) is consumed at exactly one site, runner.ts:432, inside
  CreatePrOptions, and there is no gh pr edit --add-label anywhere in the repo. The pattern
  to copy is CLAIM_LABEL in drivers/tracker/forge.ts:207-220, which already does
  add-label/remove-label against issues. Mirror it for both the gh and forgejo drivers.
* A non-terminal pr_flagged state in packages/core/src/events.ts. needs_human cannot be
  reused: it is terminal (events.ts:22-28, advances only to abandoned or done), so an
  auto-removed label would strand the task. Transitions: pr_open <-> pr_flagged,
  pr_flagged -> abandoned/done on close or merge.
* Add pr_flagged to ATTENTION_STATES (packages/dashboard/src/routes.tsx:1920) and to the
  CLI attention filter (packages/core/src/view.ts:45), which is all the surfacing it needs.
* Per-pull-request state keyed on the head SHA, so the watcher does not re-comment every
  tick on an unchanged pull request. This is the analogue of the mention watcher's
  updatedAt + lastCommentId cache.
* listOpenPrs is hardcoded to gh (pr-check.ts:36). Either keep the check GitHub-only and say
  so, or route it through PrDriver first.
design:
Flag, never close: amagi labels and comments, a human closes. The label is owned by the
watcher in both directions, which is what forces a non-terminal state rather than reusing
needs_human. Pointless pull requests accumulate until someone sweeps them; the
amagi/needs-closing label is the saved filter, and if the backlog bites the fix is a
dashboard bulk action, not auto-close. PrDriver.closePr is still built, but only a dashboard
action may call it, no watcher and no agent.
acceptance_criteria:
* An amagi-labelled open pull request whose diff against base is empty gets the amagi/needs-closing label, a PR comment with the reasoning, a tracker comment with the same reasoning, and its task moves to pr_flagged.
* A pull request without the amagi label is never flagged and never commented on, whatever its diff.
* A flagged pull request that receives real commits loses the label on the next tick and its task returns to pr_open, with no second comment.
* An unchanged flagged pull request is not re-commented on subsequent ticks.
* No code path in the watcher closes a pull request.
* pr_flagged appears in the dashboard attention list and the CLI attention view.
notes:
Depends on am-2oo.1 building the shared watcher. Do not add a fourth poll loop.
am-6ap (tracker comment when an LLM decides a pull request should be taken down) is
satisfied by the tracker-comment half of this; reconcile with that issue before starting.

title: Surface run health (context usage, cost, loop warnings) in dashboard and TUI
description: The guards are useless if the operator cannot see a run approaching them. Show per-task run health: context tokens used against the configured limit, accumulated cost, elapsed time against the budget, and any progress/loop warnings already raised. Task detail view gets the detail, the workers panel gets a compact indicator.
acceptance_criteria: Task detail view shows context usage vs limit, cost, elapsed vs budget and guard warnings; workers panel shows a compact warning marker when a run is nearing any limit; values stream through the existing event/stream plumbing rather than a new polling endpoint.

title: Fresh-context restart instead of hard kill when a guard trips
description: Killing a run that hit a context or loop guard throws away real work. Prefer a checkpoint-and-restart: ask the agent (or synthesize from the event log and worktree diff) for a short handoff summary of what is done and what remains, then start a new agent process on the same worktree with that summary as context. Cap the number of restarts per task so this cannot become its own loop.
acceptance_criteria: Restart path reuses the existing worktree and tracker claim; handoff summary persisted in the store and visible in the task view; restart count capped by config and escalates to needs_human when exhausted; covered by runner tests.

title: Per-task wall-clock and cost budgets
description:
Independent of progress heuristics, a task should have a hard ceiling on how long and how expensive it may get. The stall timeout only covers silence, and loop.maxRetries only covers transient failures, so a healthy-looking run can consume unbounded time and money. Add per-task budgets enforced by the runner across all rounds (implement, checks, review, fixes), not per agent invocation.

### How to use

Set [loop] maxRunMinutes (minutes) and/or maxCostUsd (USD) in .amagi/config.toml; 0 (the default) disables that budget. The runner counts elapsed time from the task's first claim and sums usage cost across all rounds and reclaims, stopping the agent and parking the task at needs_human with the budget figures in the reason once a limit is hit. Harnesses that report no cost (codex) skip the cost budget rather than counting zero.
acceptance_criteria: Config keys for max run duration and max cost per task; runner accumulates elapsed time and usage cost across rounds and aborts when either is exceeded; exhausted budget escalates to needs_human with the budget figures in the reason; claude usage carries cost directly, codex has none, so cost budget degrades gracefully (skipped, not treated as zero).

title: 'Run next' worker shows no title and 'model: unknown'

title: 'Run next' should allow picking harness/model/effort
description:
The 'Run next' action currently spawns a runner with no way to choose which harness, model, or effort level to use. Add an option to pick harness/model/effort (where applicable/supported) before dispatching, with necessary UI changes (e.g. a picker/dropdown in the 'Run next' flow, sensible defaults when not specified).

### How to use

- Dashboard: click "Run next" to open a picker. Choose harness (a harness.definitions name or claude/codex/opencode), model and effort; leave any field at "default" to use the configured `harness.implement`. The picker is fed by the new `GET /api/runner/options` endpoint.
- API: `POST /api/runs` now accepts optional `harness`, `model`, `effort` alongside `taskId`. Omitted fields fall back to config defaults; an unknown harness name is rejected with 409.

title: Categorize tasks by difficulty and gate high-difficulty tasks to smart models
description:
When a task is created, categorize it by difficulty (e.g. low/medium/high). High-difficulty tasks should only be pickable by 'smart' models — cheaper/weaker models should be excluded from claiming them.

Design decisions (confirmed with mpk):
- Difficulty source: auto-classified by an LLM pass over the title/description at creation time (no manual field for now).
- 'Smart model' definition: explicit model tier/allowlist in config, mapping specific model IDs to tiers (e.g. 'smart' vs 'fast'), checked against the task's difficulty.
- Enforcement point: at claim time — a worker's claim is rejected if its model's tier doesn't meet the task's difficulty bar.

Still open:
- Exact difficulty levels and the LLM classification prompt/criteria.
- Tier config schema and where model-to-tier mapping lives.
- UX for a rejected claim (error message, does the worker retry against other tasks, etc.).
### How to use

Opt in via the `[difficulty]` section in `.amagi/config.toml`:

```toml
[difficulty]
enabled = true
# explicit model id -> tier mapping; unlisted models count as the weakest tier
modelTiers = { "claude-sonnet-4-5" = "smart", "claude-haiku-4-5" = "fast" }
# minimum tier each difficulty level needs; unlisted levels need the weakest tier
requiredTier = { high = "smart" }
```

Defaults: levels low/medium/high, tiers fast/smart (weakest first), requiredTier { high = "smart" }.

When enabled:
- New tasks created from the dashboard (`POST /api/repos/:repo/issues`) or from an @agent mention "add a task" are classified by an LLM pass over the title/description using the configured implement harness; the level is stored in the task's `difficulty` metadata (beads). A classification failure leaves the task unclassified, so it is never gated.
- At claim time the worker's model must meet the task's bar: its tier must be at least `requiredTier[level]`. `amagi run` skips gated tasks and reports each as a `claim.rejected` event (a yellow "skipped ..." line); the server runner service answers 409 when asked to launch a specific gated task.
- Tasks without a difficulty are never gated.

Difficulty is opt-in: with `enabled = false` (default) no LLM pass runs and no claim is gated.

title: Add task status/activity watcher for stalled tasks
description:
Add a watcher that monitors task activity and status. Example: if a task is in 'implementing' status but has had no activity for the configured threshold (default 1h), the system should recover it automatically:

- Free/reassign the worktree the task was working on
- Reclaim the task
- Change status to pending (or similar) so it can be picked up again

Design decisions (confirmed with mpk):

- Activity signal: worker heartbeat (liveness ping from the running worker process/harness), not just log entries or status changes. Requires heartbeat plumbing if it doesn't already exist.
- Scope: watch all 'in-progress-like' statuses where a worker/session is expected to be actively doing something (implementing, reviewing, answering, etc.), not just 'implementing'.
- Threshold: configurable (per-project or global setting), default 1h.

### How to use

Enabled by default inside `amagi serve`: a per-repo stall watcher scans in-progress tasks every `loop.stallWatchIntervalSec` (default 300s) and reclaims any whose worker heartbeat is older than `loop.stallTimeoutSec` (default 3600s, 1h). Set both per-repo (`.amagi/config.toml`) or globally (`~/.config/amagi/config.toml`):

```toml
[loop]
stallTimeoutSec = 3600        # no worker activity before recovery (default 1h)
stallWatchIntervalSec = 300   # scan cadence (default 5m)
```

The worker heartbeat is the runner's liveness ping, written to the store every 60s while a task is being driven. Recovery releases the tracker claim (the issue reads ready again and any surviving runner of that task detects the lost lease and stops), then parks the task back to `claimed`, keeping its recorded worktree for the next worker to resume. It shows up in the event stream as a `task.reclaimed` event carrying the reason, and in the dashboard Workers panel as the stall-watcher's activity. `pr_open` tasks are never recovered: no worker drives them while the PR is out for review.

title: Allow chatting with worker on 'no_pr' tasks that have a summary
description:
When a task is in 'no_pr' state and has a generated summary, the UI should let the user chat with the worker about it. The worker process itself may be stale/gone, but its session should still be attachable.

Needs a design decision: on a new user message, either (a) dispatch a fresh worker on the task's selected worktree to pick up the existing session, or (b) continue/resume the existing session directly if still reachable. The chosen mechanism needs to act as a proxy to the harness for the duration of the conversation, routing messages to whichever worker/session ends up handling it.

Chosen mechanism: (a) each message dispatches a fresh harness run that resumes the task's recorded session in its preserved worktree; the answer streams back through the repo event stream.

### How to use
A 'no_pr' task with a summary, session and worktree gets a 'Chat with worker' panel on its detail page (dashboard /tasks/:id). Type a message and hit Send; the worker (resuming the original session in the task worktree) answers live in the panel. The worker's output also lands in the task agent log. Backing endpoint: POST /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/chat with { "message": "..." }, returns 202; the answer arrives as 'chat'-role agent events over the repo event stream.

title: Questions section gives no feedback after submitting an answer

title: Agent-mention watcher worker: scan PR comments/reviews for @agent, rate-limit-safe polling
description:
A dedicated, always-on worker (runs under amagi serve) that periodically scans open PRs for comments and reviews mentioning the configured agent handle, classifies each mention (fix / explain / ambiguous), and responds exactly once (comment id dedup). Extends the mention-responder logic from am-4pk.1 (which already covers classification and dedup) into a continuous worker.

## Acceptance Criteria

While amagi serve is up, the mention watcher ticks on a configurable interval (default 5 min) and reports its last activity to the dashboard Workers section. It fetches comments/reviews only for open PRs, tracks the last-seen comment per PR to avoid re-scanning old comments, and stays within GitHub REST rate limits at defaults. Each detected mention is answered at most once.

### How to use

Run `amagi serve`; the mention watcher starts automatically for every registered repo with a forge driver. It lists open PRs on a 5-minute interval (set `loop.mentionWatchIntervalSec` in the repo config to change it), fetches comments and reviews only for PRs that changed since the last scan, and responds to each human comment mentioning `forge.agentHandle` (default `@chise-maru`): fixing, explaining, logging a task, or asking for clarification. Responses are deduplicated by comment id, so each mention is answered at most once. Its last tick (last run, PRs scanned, mentions responded, errors) appears under Workers in the dashboard queue view.
notes: Builds on am-4pk.1 (classification, dedup, worktree-on-PR-branch + push path). To stay rate-limit-sane, fetch comments/reviews per open PR and remember the highest seen comment id per PR so unchanged PRs are not re-scanned; only fetch when the PR list reports activity. gh pr view --json comments,reviews gives the data; forge driver must expose read/post comments first (am-544.x).

title: PR conflict watcher: run the check-prs flow as a server worker, like mention-watcher
description:
Make the conflict half of "just check-prs" run continuously under amagi serve, the same way respond-to-mentions became the mention watcher. The mention feature has three layers; check-prs only has two, and that missing middle layer is why it never became a worker.

Mention watcher, the pattern to copy:
1. core/src/mentions.ts respondToMention(): headless, no console, onProgress callback, exec and makeHarnessFn test seams, throws on failure so the caller retries.
2. cli/src/commands/respond-to-mentions.ts: one-shot, renders onProgress to the terminal.
3. server/src/mention-watcher.ts startMentionWatcher(): self-rearming tick, per-PR skip state, activity() for the dashboard.

check-prs today:
1. core/src/pr-check.ts exports only primitives: isConflicting, listOpenPrs, prepareConflictWorktree, pushConflictFix, prMergeStatus.
2. The actual orchestration is resolveOne at cli/src/commands/check-prs.ts:26, interleaved with console.log on 11 lines, so it cannot be called from the server.
3. Nothing.

Work:
- Extract resolveOne into core as resolveConflict(), headless with an onProgress callback. Reuse the Progress class already in mentions.ts:130 rather than writing a second one; it already tracks phase, elapsed, usage and last tool.
- Rewrite cli/src/commands/check-prs.ts resolveOne as a thin renderer over it, the way respond-to-mentions.ts renders MentionProgress.
- Add server/src/pr-conflict-watcher.ts on the same shape as mention-watcher: tick, listOpenPrs, filter isConflicting against config.repo.baseBranch, dispatch resolveConflict per PR sequentially, expose activity().
- Guard re-attempts on the PR head SHA. Without it an unresolvable conflict burns a full agent run every tick. This is the analogue of the mention watchers updatedAt plus lastCommentId state.
- Add loop.prCheckIntervalSec to config.ts, mirroring loop.mentionWatchIntervalSec, default 300.

Two things block any second worker and must be done here:
- WorkerActivity (core/src/run-service.ts:29) carries mention-specific fields prsScanned and mentionsResponded. Generalize it before a second worker reports through it.
- The dashboard hardcodes those two counters at routes.tsx:989 ("scanned N PRs, responded M"). It needs to render whatever counters a worker reports.
- server/src/serve.ts:130 collects only p.mention.activity(); the existing PrPoller has no activity() at all.

Out of scope: the state-reconciliation half is already done and shipped (pr-poller.ts plus reconcilePrs). Webhooks stay out; keep the poll interface swappable.

## Acceptance Criteria

While amagi serve is up, the Workers section shows two workers, mention watcher and PR conflict watcher, each with its own last-run stamp and counters. A PR that conflicts with the base branch gets an agent dispatched within one interval, the fix is pushed to the PR head ref, and the same PR is not re-attempted until its head SHA changes. Ticks are sequential. The dispatch path is shared with check-prs.ts, not duplicated. just check passes.
### How to use

Run `amagi serve` in a repo with a forge configured. A `pr-conflict-watcher` worker joins the mention and stall watchers in the dashboard Workers section: it lists open PRs on each interval, dispatches an agent to resolve any that conflict with `repo.baseBranch`, and pushes the fix to the PR head ref. A PR is only attempted once per head SHA, so an unresolvable conflict is not retried until its head changes.

New config option `loop.prCheckIntervalSec` (default 300) controls the interval; it mirrors `loop.mentionWatchIntervalSec`. The `check-prs` CLI command shares the same resolution path.
design: The one non-obvious constraint: resolveOne cannot move to core as written because it prints as it goes. The onProgress plus Progress pattern from mentions.ts is the precedent for making an agent-dispatching flow callable from both a TTY and a headless worker, so copy it rather than inventing a second progress mechanism.
notes:
Absorbed from am-4uv, which this supersedes: the watcher must be toggleable on and off (a [conflict] or [loop] config key plus a dashboard control), and its recent activity should be visible on the dashboard, not just a last-run stamp.

Warning about am-4uv: its description carries an agent-written "### How to use" section claiming a [conflict] enabled = true config key and a dashboard Conflict toggle already exist. Neither does. config.ts has no conflict section, packages/server/src has no conflict runner, and the word conflict appears nowhere in packages/dashboard/src. Do not treat that text as a description of existing behaviour.

title: Dedicated workers: PR checker and agent-mention watcher
description:
The dashboard Workers section should show two dedicated, always-on workers instead of only the task-runner pool:

1. PR checker: periodically inspects open PRs (merge-conflict status, state reconciliation) and dispatches the agent on conflict, extending the existing conflict runner (am-4uv) and check-prs flow.
2. Agent-mention watcher: periodically scans PR comments/reviews for the configured agent handle, classifies each mention, and responds, extending the poller in am-4pk.1.

Both must run continuously under amagi serve, report their status in the dashboard Workers section, and poll at intervals that respect GitHub rate limits (no hammering the API).

## Success Criteria

The Workers section shows two workers (PR checker, mention watcher) as actively working while amagi serve is up. Each worker has a sane, configurable poll interval, does not exceed GitHub rate limits at default settings, and surfaces its last activity in the dashboard.
notes: Clusters the existing in-progress poller work (am-4uv conflict runner, am-4pk.1 mention responder) into visible, always-on dedicated workers with a shared dashboard home and rate-limit-aware polling. Webhooks are the eventual replacement for polling; keep the worker interface swappable but do not build webhook support now.

title: Toggle full task details in /tasks/:id view
description:
TaskDetailView (packages/dashboard/src/routes.tsx) currently shows only operational fields: tracker, agent, model, effort, usage, worktree, branch, PR, session, error. The underlying issue metadata that bv (beads viewer) shows for the same task - description, acceptance criteria, priority, type, assignee, labels, dependencies, parent - is not visible there.

Add a toggle (show/hide) in the /tasks/:id view that renders the full issue details, matching what bv displays. The issues data is already available via the tracker API used by IssuesView (GET /api/repos/:repo/issues), which returns the full Issue shape including description and acceptanceCriteria.

### How to use

Open a task in the dashboard at /tasks/:id (any task in the Queue view). Below the operational fields (tracker, agent, model, usage, worktree, branch, PR, session, error) is a "show issue details" button. Click it to fetch the issue from the existing tracker API (GET /api/repos/:repo/issues/:id) and render the full issue metadata: priority, type, assignee, labels, parent, blocked-by dependencies, description, and acceptance criteria, styled like the Tasks view issue detail. Click "hide issue details" to collapse it back. Requires a repository to be selected; the button is hidden otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: The /tasks/:id view has a toggle that reveals the full issue details: description, acceptance criteria, priority, type, assignee, labels, dependencies, parent. The detail matches what bv shows for the same issue, and the data comes from the existing tracker issues API, no new endpoint required.

Show a last action time (and/or per-line timestamps) in the log view, derived from the existing ts on each AgentLogLine, so a task that stopped producing output is obvious.

title: no_pr tasks that are actually complete get force-closed as abandoned instead of done
description:
Currently a no_pr task (packages/core/src/runner.ts:353-359, agent produced no changes) can only be retired via the Close button (packages/dashboard/src/routes.tsx CloseButton, ~line 1135), which POSTs /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/close (packages/server/src/app.ts:348-385). That endpoint always transitions to 'abandoned' (events.ts FORWARD: no_pr -> [abandoned] only). This is wrong when the agent left no changes *because the task was already done* — the operator (or an LLM judging the no_pr statusReason) has no way to mark it 'done' instead of 'abandoned'. 'abandoned' semantically means the work was given up on, not that it was already satisfied.

Two options to resolve, pick one (or both):
1. Automatic: when the no_pr transition reason indicates the agent is certain the task was already complete (see whyNoChangesPrompt / runner.ts:334-360), let the runner or a reviewing pass transition straight to 'done' instead of leaving it parked in 'no_pr' for manual abandon.
2. Manual: add a second action alongside the existing Close button (which should keep abandoning) — e.g. a 'Mark done' button/endpoint for no_pr (and possibly needs_human) tasks that transitions to 'done' with an operator-supplied reason, mirroring the existing close flow but choosing state 'done' instead of 'abandoned'.

Needs: events.ts canTransition/FORWARD to permit no_pr/needs_human -> done; a server endpoint (new route or extend /close with a target state param); dashboard button wiring. Check packages/core/src/runner.test.ts and packages/server/src/app.test.ts for existing close/abandon coverage to extend.

### How to use

A no_pr/needs_human task can now be retired as `done` instead of only `abandoned`. In the dashboard, parked tasks show a green "Mark done" button next to "Close": both prompt for a reason, then POST `/api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/close` with `{ reason, to }` (`to: "done"` vs the default `"abandoned"`). Marking done records the task.state transition no_pr/needs_human -> done and closes the tracker issue; the existing Close button keeps abandoning. The endpoint rejects `to: "done"` from any non-parked state.
acceptance_criteria: A no_pr (and ideally needs_human) task that was actually already complete can be closed as 'done' via the dashboard without going through 'abandoned'. Existing abandon-via-Close behavior is unchanged. Tests cover the new transition path.

title: Worker ends runs with no changes and no summary when it cannot read tracker notes or beads from the worktree
description:
Symptom: worker for am-ccg (session ses_f3c713dc6ffeGeLf1MDnDjDbqk, opencode + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) ended the run with zero changes, zero tool output that investigated the bug, and no LLM summary. The no_pr reason fell back to the canned string "the agent produced no changes; the task may already be done". The task description explicitly asked to "determine whether this is a bug in how amagi invokes biome ... and fix accordingly", yet the agent never reproduced the crash, never touched the crash worktree, and made no code change.

Root causes found by investigation (evidence from the events store):

1. The implement prompt never includes task notes. implementPrompt (packages/core/src/prompt.ts) passes only task title + description, never task.notes. am-ccg's notes already contained the root cause (biome 2.5.14 panic=abort on EPIPE when output is piped through head/tail) and the planned fix (prompt rule), but the agent could not see them.

2. bd does not work inside worktrees. The worktree .beads has no dolt database and no redirect file to the main repo's .beads, so `bd show am-ccg` inside the worktree fails with "no beads database found". The agent therefore could not re-read the issue (notes, comments) from within the worktree. The main repo's real DB lives in .beads/embeddeddolt (bd where).

3. With both blind spots, the agent inferred "already done" from git state alone: working tree clean, branch behind origin/main, `git log origin/main..HEAD` empty. It produced no final summary, so runner.ts no_pr handling fell back to the canned reason.

4. The fix recorded in am-ccg's notes (a rule in implementSystemPrompt telling agents not to pipe lint/check output through head/tail) exists only as an uncommitted working-tree edit on main (packages/core/src/prompt.ts lines 23-24) with no commit and no PR; am-ccg itself is still in_progress/no_pr.

Proposed work to make "do nothing" impossible or at least accountable:

- Include task.notes (and comments) in the implement prompt so prior analysis and planned fixes are visible to the agent.
- Make tracker context available in the worktree: either point worktree .beads at the main repo DB (redirect file) or embed the full issue text in the prompt so the agent never needs bd.
- Enforce that a no-change outcome carries an agent-written report/summary (am-exb/#60 made the reason carry the summary when present, but an agent that writes no summary still falls through to the canned string).
- For investigation-style descriptions ("determine whether ... and fix accordingly"), a clean git state must not be treated as "already done"; the agent should still deliver findings.
- Land the prompt.ts head/tail rule from am-ccg's notes as a committed change/PR and close am-ccg.

title: Investigate biome crash (SIGABRT) when running biome check in worker worktree
description:
Potential bug: biome crashes with SIGABRT (signal 6, core dump) when a worker runs 'biome check .' inside a worktree.

Observed process:
PID 345621 (biome), UID 1000 (mpk), Signal 6 (ABRT), on host esther, Mon 2026-09-21 10:32:45 CEST.

Command Line: /home/mpk/.cache/amagi/worktrees/amagi-am-0c3-dashboard-close-needs-human-no/node_modules/.bun/@biomejs+cli-linux-x64@2.5.14/node_modules/@biomejs/cli-linux-x64/biome check .
Executable: .../@biomejs/cli-linux-x64/biome
Core dump: /var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.biome.1000...345621...zst (4.6M)

Note: the worktree name (amagi-am-0c3-dashboard-close-needs-human-no) matches task am-0c3, so this happened while a worker was working on that task.

Determine whether this is a bug in how amagi invokes biome (args, cwd, env, missing input) or a biome issue, and fix accordingly.
notes:
Root cause: not an amagi invocation bug. biome 2.5.14 (latest) panics with panic=abort on BrokenPipe: `unwrap()` on stdout write at crates/biome_console/src/lib.rs:173:14. Trigger: agents run `bun run lint 2>&1 | head/tail -N` inside worktrees; head exits after N lines, biome gets EPIPE, aborts. amagi's own runChecks reads biome stdout to EOF and never triggers it. Fix: added a rule to implementSystemPrompt telling agents not to pipe check/lint output through head/tail (redirect to a file instead). Reproduced locally: `bun run lint 2>&1 | head -3` produces an identical coredump.
Fix implemented: added the head/tail rule to implementSystemPrompt (packages/core/src/prompt.ts) plus a prompt.test.ts assertion. Verified: just check passes (typecheck, lint, build, 398 tests). Not an amagi invocation bug; biome's panic=abort on BrokenPipe is only reachable via agent-side piping, now banned by prompt rule.

title: PR conflict runner: periodic check + worker dispatch, toggleable, dashboard status
description:
Add a runner to the server that periodically checks current pull requests for conflicts. If a conflict is detected it should try to dispatch a worker to fix it.

Requirements:
- periodic check of current PRs for merge conflicts
- on conflict detection, dispatch a worker to fix it
- the runner must be toggleable (can be turned on/off)
- visible status on the dashboard showing what the runner is currently doing
- visible logs of the runner's activity on the dashboard

### How to use

The conflict runner is part of `amagi serve` and is bound to the repo the server is launched from. It is **off by default**.

To enable at startup, set `[conflict] enabled = true` in the repo's `.amagi/config.toml`. At runtime, toggle it from the dashboard: the **Conflict runner** panel on the Queue page shows the current state (on/off/working), the last check time, the conflicting/open PR counts, and the runner's activity log, with an Enable/Disable button.

While enabled, every 60s the runner lists the repo's open PRs, finds the ones conflicting against the base branch, and dispatches a resolution agent for each (same flow as `amagi check-prs`): it merges the base into a worktree on the PR head, has the agent resolve the conflicts, and pushes the fix back to the PR head ref. Ticks are sequential, so a long resolution delays the next check rather than stacking.

The state and activity log are also exposed over the API:
- `GET /api/conflict-runner` returns `{ enabled, working, lastCheckAt, checkedPrs, conflicting, logs }`
- `POST /api/conflict-runner` with `{ "enabled": true|false }` toggles it and returns the same status

title: Dashboard: close needs_human/no_pr tasks with reason
description:
There is no way from the dashboard to say 'this task does not need more work' for a needs_human/no_pr task; the operator has to close the underlying bd/tracker issue by hand. Tracker.close(id, reason) already exists unconditionally on the Tracker interface (packages/core/src/drivers/types.ts) and is already used by reconcile.ts (~line 39) when a PR merges.

Add POST /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/close that:
- accepts an operator-supplied reason
- transitions the task to abandoned recording that reason (feeds am-b2z.11's statusReason)
- calls tracker.close(id, reason)

Add a Close button with a reason prompt to TaskDetailView for needs_human/no_pr tasks, and to the Needs attention rows on QueueView.

title: Settings UI with worker-count field, validated and live-applied
description:
There is no settings UI in the dashboard. Add one, with at least one field: the number of workers (concurrent task runs).

Current wiring:
- Worker count = config.loop.maxParallel (int, min 1, default 1) at packages/core/src/config.ts:64, loaded from .amagi/config.toml by loadConfig.
- The server builds one RunService per repo at startup; its capacity is a readonly field set once in the constructor from config.loop.maxParallel (packages/core/src/run-service.ts:50). The dashboard shows capacity via /api/runner (routes.tsx Workers header).
- The Workspaces cache also builds config once per repo (packages/core/src/workspace.ts build()).

Wanted:
1. A settings page/section in the dashboard.
2. A worker-count field that is validated to a reasonable range (already int min 1 via the zod schema; decide a sensible upper bound and enforce it both in the UI and server-side, e.g. reject <=0 or absurd values so nothing can set 0 workers or a runaway number).
3. Applying it updates both the backend (RunService capacity must become mutable/live, since it is currently readonly-at-construction) and the UI (capacity shown in the Workers header) without restarting the server or exploding running tasks. If changing config on disk, decide the write path (currently config is read-only TOML; may need a writer or an in-memory override endpoint).
4. Changing the value must not kill or lose in-flight runs; new capacity only affects new launches.

Related: am-8wd (kanban/dashboard with auto-pick, worker slots).

title: just run should allow picking harness + model directly from the CLI
description:
Running 'just run' currently goes through the interactive harness/model picker (select-run.ts) when a TTY is present. It should be possible to pick the harness and model directly from the command line, e.g. 'just run -- --harness claude --model <model>' (or a justfile alias), so the run is scriptable and the interactive prompt can be skipped entirely. Related: am-bcw (claude/codex models missing from the list) and am-u7f (hardcode claude/codex model options from config instead of CLI scraping). Check what CLI args run.ts already exposes and what is missing, then make harness+model selection work non-interactively.

### How to use

`just run` now forwards harness/model/effort flags to `amagi run`, so the interactive picker can be skipped and the run scripted:

```bash
just run -- --harness claude --model <model>
just run --harness codex --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort high
```

Both forms are equivalent (the `--` only stops `just` from parsing the flags itself); `--harness` also accepts a `harness.definitions` name. With no flags, `just run` keeps the previous behavior: interactive picker on a TTY, `harness.implement` defaults otherwise.

title: No-PR outcome should carry an LLM summary, not a canned reason

title: Investigate hung task am-fum; add interrupt/restart for tasks
description:
am-fum (interactive picker for 'bun run ... run') has been hung for a long time; the machine froze and needed a hard restart (lease expired, heartbeat stopped ~25 min ago).

Investigate why the task hung (did the harness hang, or was the whole machine the cause?).

Also, in cases like this there should be a way to 'interrupt' a hung task and 'start' it again: either resume via 'continue', or restart the task with a different harness/model.

### Findings: why am-fum hung

The hang was a whole-machine freeze, not a harness hang. Evidence from the
pre-freeze store, the opencode log and the system journal:

- am-fum's opencode harness streamed normally until 01:40:57 local, then went
  silent mid-turn: the last log line is `llm runtime selected` as it started an
  LLM request to the (remote) `aiapi.enigma.com.pl` API. No `agent.exited`
  event, no error, task parked in `implementing`.
- The compositor (niri) began logging "system too slow" and input lag of
  660ms at 01:40:59, one second after the agent went silent, and kept lagging
  until the hard reboot at 01:46:27. The whole desktop froze, which is a
  system-level event, not an agent process hang.
- The model is served remotely, so the harness was not running local inference
  or burning local RAM/GPU. The contributing pressure was the general system
  load (firefox with many tabs, multiple agent processes, a ~2GB shared
  opencode SQLite DB) under memory/swap pressure on a work laptop.

The harness was a victim of the freeze, not its cause. The store-based lease
recovery then worked as designed: after the reboot the lease lapsed, bd
returned the task to ready, the runner re-claimed it in the same worktree and
completed it (PR #121). What was missing was a way to interrupt a hung run
deliberately and restart it from the CLI/API.

### How to use

Interrupt a hung task and start it again, in the same worktree:

```bash
amagi stop bd-1234        # park the run in `cancelled`; a live runner kills its agent process
amagi continue bd-1234    # resume in the recorded worktree with the configured harness
amagi continue bd-1234 --harness opencode --model local/...   # same worktree, different harness/model
```

`amagi stop <id>` appends a `task.state` transition to `cancelled` (or use
`POST /api/tasks/:id/stop`). A running runner watches the store, kills the
agent process and unwinds; a crashed runner leaves the task parked in
`cancelled`. `amagi continue <id>` re-claims the task and drives it in the
worktree and branch already recorded for it, so no work is lost; pass
`--harness`/`--model` to restart with a different harness or model.
`POST /api/tasks/:id/reclaim` also resumes a `cancelled` task for the
dashboard.

title: Respond to @agent mentions on pull requests
description: The only agent-triggered PR action today is merge-conflict resolution (check-prs.ts). When a human reviews an amagi PR and pings the agent account in a comment or review (e.g. @chise-maru), nothing happens. AMBIGUOUS mentions ask a clarifying question through the question channel before acting. Deduplicate by comment id so a mention is answered once.
acceptance_criteria: A mention of the configured agent handle in a PR comment or review is picked up by the poller, classified as fix/explain/ambiguous, and answered at most once (comment id dedup). A fix request produces a commit pushed to the PR branch addressing the feedback. An explain request posts an answer comment. An ambiguous mention asks a clarifying question instead of acting. The forge driver can read and post PR comments (gh now, tea as part of am-544.3). Tests cover classification and dedup.

The agent handle must be configured (e.g. config.forge.agentHandle, currently @chise-maru) not hardcoded. Share the worktree-on-PR-branch + push path with check-prs.ts. Surfacing the detected mention and the response in the dashboard can follow later; the poller pattern in server/src/pr-poller.ts is the home for the watch loop.

title: Label pull requests opened by amagi
description: amagi PRs are currently created without any labels, so a human scanning the forge cannot tell agent-generated PRs apart from their own or filter them by intent. Define a small, namespaced label scheme and apply it when the runner opens a PR. Proposed scheme: an 'amagi' provenance label marking the PR as agent-generated, plus an 'amagi/<type>' label mirroring the source beads task type (feature, bug, chore, task, epic) so reviewers can triage by intent. Labels are created on demand (best effort, same pattern as CLAIM_LABEL in drivers/tracker/forge.ts) and added at PR creation time in drivers/pr.ts; the tea driver covers it as part of am-544.3.

The gh driver applies labels at createPr time and tests cover derivation plus the gh flags used. The tea driver applies the same labels as part of am-544.3.
notes: Branch name already encodes the task id (amagi/<taskId>-<slug>, worktree.ts:35) and the PR body carries the task id, so the type label is the only new source needed: the tracker task already exposes type. Prefixing type labels with 'amagi/' keeps them distinct from human labels.

title: Reclaim a failed task from the dashboard
description: When a run dies mid-flight (power loss, VPN down, harness crash) the task freezes in a non-terminal state (e.g. implementing) in the store with a recorded worktree and branch, and there is no way to resume it from the UI. Add a manual reclaim action: a human pushes a stuck task back into the queue, the runner reuses the recorded worktree and branch instead of creating a fresh one, and starts a new harness turn that is told to continue the existing work.
acceptance_criteria: A failed/stuck task with a recorded worktree shows a Reclaim action on its detail page. The action returns the task to a claimable state. When picked up, the runner reuses the recorded worktree and branch rather than creating a new one. The resumed agent is given context that it is continuing existing work and can complete the task and open a PR normally. Tests cover the endpoint, the state transition, and worktree reuse.
notes: Trigger observed in the field: task am-3ga showed 'agent failed: exit1' after power died and the VPN dropped (no deepseek access). The agent-failed path in runner.ts:364 only appends a non-fatal error and keeps going; when the amagi process itself dies the task just freezes mid-state with its worktree/branch still recorded in the store. Overlap: am-eey.10 covers retry-now/abandon for deferred automatic retries; am-eey.9 covers runner-side worktree reuse for auto-retried tasks. Implement the worktree/branch reuse in the runner so both this manual path and am-eey.9 share it.

title: Dashboard /issues never shows closed tasks
description:
The /issues view filters on status (open/in_progress/blocked/closed) but closed tasks never appear.

Root cause: the beads tracker driver list() in packages/core/src/drivers/tracker/beads.ts:131 runs `bd list --json --limit 200` without --all. bd list excludes closed issues unless --all is passed (verified: plain bd list returns only in_progress, `bd list --status=closed` returns 42). The server endpoint GET /api/repos/:repo/issues (packages/server/src/app.ts:288) just returns ws.listIssues(), so closed issues never reach the dashboard; the Closed option in the status select (packages/dashboard/src/routes.tsx:617) and the closed kanban column can never show anything.

Fix direction: add --all to the list() invocation in the beads driver (or filter appropriately), so the API/dashboard receive closed issues too. Confirm dashboard still renders closed items (badge, column) and pagination handles the larger set.

title: Resource usage viewer per runner
description:
The dashboard shows a Workers section (routes.tsx, one row per slot from /api/runner) but it only reports running task ids and capacity, not resource usage. With multiple runners (RunService instances, one per repo, each running up to loop.maxParallel tasks), there is no way to see how many resources each runner is actually consuming.

Wanted: a per-runner resource usage view, showing at least CPU and memory (and ideally RSS, CPU time, and child-process totals) for each active runner, so the operator can see which runner is eating the machine.

Current building blocks:
- Each runner holds an AgentProcess with a pid (packages/core/src/drivers/types.ts:140, harness spawn.ts:97).
- packages/core/src/process.ts already has processTree(pid) / childPids(pid) helpers used for killTree; these can enumerate the whole agent process tree per runner.
- /api/runner returns RunnerStatus (available/capacity/running ids) from RunService.status(); the server has one runner per repo, so the endpoint needs a per-repo or per-runner shape to tell them apart.

Design notes to resolve during implementation: whether resource data comes from process.resourceUsage (this process only) vs reading /proc/<pid>/stat + /proc/<pid>/status per pid in the tree and summing; how often to sample (polling endpoint vs periodic snapshot into the store); and how the dashboard renders it (per-runner cards/rows in the Workers section or the Sessions view).

title: Show deferred retries and recovery actions
description:
Make the dashboard distinguish deferred automatic retries from actual human intervention. Show the retry time and failure reason, and provide explicit retry-now and abandon actions for recoverable tasks.

### How to use

When a transient harness failure (quota, rate limit, overloaded model, flaky network) defers a task, it parks in the `retrying` state instead of needing a human.

- The Board gets a separate orange **Retrying** column (no longer lumped into In progress), and every retrying card shows when the next attempt fires (e.g. "retries in 45s") and the failure reason.
- A retrying task is absent from Overview/Inbox **Needs attention**, and its detail page shows a "Deferred automatic retry" panel with the retry countdown and reason.
- **Retry now** button (task detail, retrying tasks only): skips the remaining backoff and starts the next attempt immediately. Backed by `POST /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/retry`; answers 409 unless the task is deferring a retry.
- **Close** (task detail, retrying tasks only): abandons the task, stopping the backoff, deleting the worktree and closing the tracker issue as abandoned. The Reclaim button is hidden on retrying tasks because the runner still owns them.
acceptance_criteria: Deferred tasks are absent from Needs attention, show their scheduled retry and reason, and retry-now and abandon produce valid state transitions with tests.
